children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start with the first step. To check your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to know about the child or children you're claiming for.

**How old is the child you want to claim Child Benefit for?**

Please tell me:
- The child's age (or date of birth)
- If you have more than one child, I'll need to check each one

The age is important because eligibility depends on whether the child is:
- **Under 16 years old** (usually automatically eligible)
- **16-19 years old** (depends on education or training status)
- **20 or over** (not eligible for Child Benefit)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I want to claim Child Benefit for my son Alex. He's 9 years old, so still quite young. It's just the one child I'm asking about.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! That's helpful to know.

So you want to claim Child Benefit for **Alex, who is 9 years old**. Since Alex is under 16, he falls into the automatic qualification category. Let me navigate to the next check in the process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! Now I need to check one more thing:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work at all)?**

At 9 years old, most children wouldn't be in full-time paid work, but I need to confirm this for the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work at all - he's only 9! He's still in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's exactly what I expected. Alex is in primary school and not working, so he meets that requirement. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Next question:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in their own right?**

Specifically, I'm checking if Alex is receiving:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA), or
- Universal Credit

in his own name. At 9 years old, this would be unusual, but I need to confirm for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a kid - I don't think 9-year-olds can claim those things anyway!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: You're absolutely right! At 9 years old, Alex wouldn't be claiming those benefits. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Next question:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

Given that Alex is only 9 years old and in primary school, I suspect the answer is no. But let me confirm - is he in any kind of apprenticeship programme?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, definitely not! He's only 9 - he's in primary school, not doing any apprenticeship or anything like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! At 9 years old and in primary school, Alex clearly isn't in an apprenticeship. Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check your residency situation. This is an important requirement for Child Benefit eligibility.

**Do you meet the UK residency requirements?**

There are several ways you might qualify. Let me check which applies to your situation:

1. **Do you normally live in the UK?** (This is the most common route)

Or do any of these apply to you:
- You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?
- You have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme (and meet certain conditions around work, job-seeking, studying, or having sufficient resources)?
- You're a Crown servant living abroad?

What's your residency situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, I don't live in the UK at the moment. I'm living abroad right now.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Okay, thank you for clarifying that. You're living abroad. Let me ask a few more questions to understand your situation better, as there are still some ways you might qualify for Child Benefit even if you're not normally resident in the UK.

**Can you tell me more about your situation abroad:**

1. **Are you a Crown servant living abroad?** (For example, working for the UK government, military, or in a qualifying country on behalf of the UK)

2. **Or do you have a visa/residency status from the EU Settlement Scheme?** (Either settled status or pre-settled status)

3. **If neither of those, do you have any other special connection to the UK** that might mean you still qualify?

These details will help me determine if you can still be eligible for Child Benefit while living abroad.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not a Crown servant or anything like that. I don't have any special EU settlement status either. I just moved abroad - nothing special about my situation, really.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I appreciate your honesty about your situation.

Unfortunately, based on the eligibility requirements, if you're living abroad and don't meet any of the special residency pathways (such as being a Crown servant, having EU Settlement Scheme status, or normally living in the UK), you would not qualify for Child Benefit at this time.

However, let me confirm the decision with you:

**You are currently living abroad with no special residency status, and you want to claim Child Benefit for Alex (age 9).**

Based on the UK Child Benefit eligibility rules, the residency requirement is a fundamental part of eligibility. You must normally live in the UK or meet one of the special circumstances to qualify.

Before I provide my final assessment, I want to ask:

**Are you planning to move back to the UK?** If so, that could change your eligibility. Child Benefit eligibility is assessed based on your current circumstances, so if you're returning to the UK soon, that would be an important factor.

Or if you're unsure about whether your situation might fall under any special circumstances, I'm happy to explore that further.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not planning to move back to the UK anytime soon. I'm settled where I am for now.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that clarification. Based on your circumstances, I can now provide you with my final eligibility assessment.

conversation.text:
## **Assessment Result: NOT ELIGIBLE FOR CHILD BENEFIT**

---

**Summary for Alex (age 9):**

I'm sorry to tell you that **you are not currently eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**, even though Alex himself meets all the child-specific eligibility requirements.

**Why you're not eligible:**

The key issue is the **residency requirement**. To qualify for Child Benefit, the person claiming (you, the parent) must normally live in the UK or meet special circumstances such as:
- Being a Crown servant living abroad, or
- Having settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme

Since you're living abroad without any of these special statuses, you don't meet the residency requirement for Child Benefit eligibility.

**Good news about Alex:**
Alex himself meets all the eligibility criteria perfectly:
- ✓ Age 9 (under 16)
- ✓ In education (primary school)
- ✓ Not in paid work
- ✓ Not receiving disqualifying benefits
- ✓ Not in a disqualifying apprenticeship

**What you can do:**

If and when you return to the UK in the future, you would be able to reapply for Child Benefit for Alex. At that point, as long as Alex is still under 16 (or meets the education requirements if aged 16-19), you should be eligible.

For more information, you can visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility

Is there anything else I can help clarify about this decision?

reasonings: Alex is 9 years old, which would normally make him automatically eligible for Child Benefit as he is under 16. He is in primary school, not in paid work, and does not receive benefits in his own right or in a disqualifying apprenticeship. However, the claimant (Alex's parent) does not meet the UK residency requirement for Child Benefit. The claimant is living abroad and does not have any of the special residency statuses that would allow them to claim (such as being a Crown servant abroad, having EU Settlement Scheme status, or normally living in the UK). Without meeting the residency requirement, the claimant is ineligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex, despite Alex himself meeting all the child-specific eligibility criteria.
arguments.overall_reasoning: Although Alex meets all the criteria related to the child (age under 16, in education, not working, not receiving disqualifying benefits), the claimant does not meet the fundamental residency requirement for Child Benefit. The claimant is living abroad with no special circumstances that would qualify them under the residency rules. Therefore, the family is not eligible for Child Benefit at this time. If the claimant returns to the UK in the future, they would be able to reapply."
